sections.html:
By land area, Suffolk is the largest city in Virginia, with about 399 square miles of land and another 30 of water. It lies in Hampton Roads along the Nansemond and James rivers and holds part of the Great Dismal Swamp. A downtown, a northern corridor tied to defense work and long rural stretches all fall inside the city line, and 27.1% of residents lived in areas the census counted as rural in 2020.

A Suffolk house can therefore be a downtown bungalow, a home near Harborview in the north or a farmhouse on a country road. Each sells differently.

Suffolk was founded in 1742 as a port on the Nansemond River, first called Constant's Warehouse. It incorporated as a city in 1910. In 1974 it merged with the independent city of Nansemond, which had been Nansemond County until 1972, and the merger brought in the towns of Holland and Whaleyville.

The city is now divided into seven boroughs: Chuckatuck, Cypress, Holy Neck, Nansemond, Sleepy Hole, Suffolk and Whaleyville. They are political districts, not neighborhoods, but sellers often use the borough or the old community name to say where a house is.

sections.h2: Work and employers behind the market
sections.html:
Distribution, manufacturing, farming, health care and defense work support the economy. Peanut processing has been a local industry for over a century, and Planters Peanuts began in the city in 1912. Sentara Obici Hospital, completed in 2002 as Louise Obici Memorial Hospital, is a major health employer.

Defense contractors and Navy commands cluster in the north end near US 17 and Interstate 664. The Joint Forces Command base there was disestablished in 2011, and some of its functions continued in the same buildings. Those jobs mean buyers and sellers who move on orders, so timing matters.

Suffolk is served by US 13, 17, 58, 258 and 460, State Route 10 and Interstate 664, which crosses the northeastern edge. The Monitor-Merrimac Memorial Bridge-Tunnel, completed in 1992, links the city to Newport News. The city took over its own road system from the Virginia Department of Transportation on July 1, 2006, so roads and drainage ditches are now a city responsibility.

Water matters here. A house near the Nansemond, the swamp or low farmland may sit in a flood zone, and buyers or their insurers will ask. Check FEMA's flood map for your parcel before you talk to any buyer.

Summers are hot and humid and winters are mild to cool. Normals for 1991 to 2020 show about 51.8 inches of rain a year, with July highs near 87 degrees and a record of 105.

  • More than 120 days a year bring measurable rain, which tests gutters, grading and crawl spaces.
  • Snow is light, about 5.8 inches a year, so winter roof loads are rarely the worry.
  • Humidity is the steady problem, showing up as mold, wood rot and failing HVAC systems.

Those are the repairs a cash buyer prices in, and the ones a conventional buyer's inspector will list.

Suffolk Public Schools runs 12 elementary schools, four middle schools, three high schools and one alternative school. Nansemond-Suffolk Academy is a private college preparatory school, and Paul D. Camp Community College has a campus in the city. Suffolk Transit is the local bus service, with two connections to Hampton Roads Transit buses, but most commuters drive.

Local attractions include the Seaboard Station Railroad Museum at 326 North Main Street, Riddick's Folly, the Suffolk Historic District and the Driver Historic District, and the Peanut Fest each fall, a tradition since 1977. Mention the schools and the commute when you talk to a buyer, since both are usual questions.

sections.h2: What a Suffolk seller pays at closing
sections.html:
Virginia's deed taxes apply in Suffolk as anywhere else in the state. The state recordation tax is 25 cents per $100 under section 58.1-801, and the grantor's tax is 50 cents per $500 under section 58.1-802. The grantor's tax falls on the seller, and the clerk who records the deed splits it between the state and the locality.

  • Request a title search early so liens surface before the closing date.
  • Confirm tax proration on the settlement statement.
  • Keep copies of the deed, the closing statement and the payoff letters.
  • Ask the Suffolk Treasurer or Commissioner of the Revenue for real estate tax dates.

Special rules can apply. The Residential Property Disclosure Act excludes transfers by a fiduciary during the administration of an estate, guardianship, conservatorship or trust, under section 55.1-702. Foreclosure sales and sales between spouses or to family in the direct line are also excluded. An estate attorney can tell you whether your sale falls inside the list.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works in Suffolk
sections.html:
The contract, title search and deed are the same as in any Virginia sale, without the buyer's lender.

  • Tell us about the house, its condition and your timeline.
  • We review the property, and any offer reflects the house as it stands.
  • A closing company searches the title and prepares the deed.
  • You sign, receive your proceeds and hand over the keys.

Bring a photo ID, the deed if you have one and mortgage details. Taxes and liens are paid from your proceeds at the table.

sections.h2: When is a cash sale the right choice?
sections.html:
A cash sale suits houses that would struggle in a financed sale, such as one with storm damage, deferred maintenance, tenants or title questions. It also helps owners who live out of the area, since there is little to coordinate.

It is not the only good route. A listing can bring more money for a house in strong condition, if you can wait and pay for repairs. Compare the final net, not the headline offer.

faqs.q: Is Suffolk the biggest city in Virginia?
faqs.a: By land area, yes. Suffolk has about 399 square miles of land, the most of any city in the state.
Suffolk has seven boroughs: Chuckatuck, Cypress, Holy Neck, Nansemond, Sleepy Hole, Suffolk and Whaleyville. They are political districts used for city council and school board seats.

faqs.q: Do I need to repair my Suffolk house before selling for cash?
faqs.a: No. Cash buyers generally buy as is, so you can skip repairs and cleaning. A listing usually needs repairs to satisfy buyers' inspections and lenders.

faqs.q: Who pays Virginia's grantor's tax on a Suffolk sale?
faqs.a: The seller does unless the parties agree otherwise. The tax is 50 cents per $500 of value under Virginia Code 58.1-802.

faqs.q: How many people live in Suffolk, Virginia?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 94,324 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 104,699.
